name: MCP Tool Router
content:
"""
title: MCP Tool Router
description: One connection instead of many — search the tools of all running MCP instances, fetch a schema, call it. Keeps the tool list in the prompt small. Read-only.
author: Torsten Feustel
version: 0.0.9
license: MIT
category: System
"""

import difflib
import inspect
import logging
import time
import unicodedata
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Any

import httpx
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

# One line per call. Without it, the only way to tell whether a model follows
# find → describe → call is to reconstruct it from the runner's network
# traffic — which is exactly as tedious as it sounds.
logger = logging.getLogger("mcp_tool_router")

# Hard-coded so a copy installed under a different ID still cannot route into
# itself: any instance offering exactly these three tools is a router.
SELF_ID = "mcp_tool_router"
SELF_FINGERPRINT = {"find_tools", "describe_tools", "call_tool"}
UMLAUTS = {"ä": "ae", "ö": "oe", "ü": "ue", "ß": "ss"}


def _norm(word: str) -> str:
    """Lowercase, umlauts spelled out, accents dropped.

    German and English descriptions sit side by side in one installation, so a
    raw substring match misses half the catalog.
    """
    out = word.lower()
    for source, target in UMLAUTS.items():
        out = out.replace(source, target)
    out = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", out)
    return "".join(c for c in out if not unicodedata.combining(c))


def _first_line(text: str, limit: int = 140) -> str:
    """First sentence-ish of a docstring, collapsed to one line."""
    line = (text or "").strip().split("\n")[0].strip()
    return line[: limit - 1] + "…" if len(line) > limit else line


@asynccontextmanager
async def _mcp_streams(url: str, headers: dict, timeout: int):
    """Read/write streams to an MCP endpoint — across both SDK generations.

    mcp 2.x renamed the transport, moved headers and timeout onto an HTTP
    client that is handed to it, and yields two streams where 1.x yielded
    three. This same tool JSON also runs inside OpenWebUI, whose SDK version is
    not ours to pin, so both shapes stay supported.
    """
    from mcp.client import streamable_http as transport

    opener = getattr(transport, "streamable_http_client", None)
    if opener is not None and "http_client" in inspect.signature(opener).parameters:
        # mcp >= 1.29: headers no longer go to the transport but to an HTTP
        # client handed to it — and 2.x swapped the library that client comes
        # from (httpx2). Take it from the transport module rather than guess.
        http_lib = getattr(transport, "httpx2", None) or getattr(transport, "httpx", None)
        if http_lib is None:  # pragma: no cover - neither name present
            import httpx as http_lib
        async with http_lib.AsyncClient(headers=headers, timeout=timeout) as client:
            async with opener(url, http_client=client) as (read, write, *_):
                yield read, write
        return

    # Older 1.x: headers and timeout go straight to the transport, and it
    # yields a third element nobody here needs.
    async with transport.streamablehttp_client(
        url, headers=headers, timeout=timeout
    ) as (read, write, *_):
        yield read, write


class Tools:
    class Valves(BaseModel):
        manager_url: str = Field(
            default="http://127.0.0.1:7860",
            description="Base URL of the MCP spawner (manager API)",
        )
        auth_token: str = Field(
            default="",
            description="Bearer token for the manager API — use the read-only token from Settings, not the password",
        )
        mcp_token: str = Field(
            default="",
            description="Bearer token of the MCP endpoints (leave empty if none)",
        )
        mcp_base_url: str = Field(
            default="",
            description=(
                "Optional override. Empty = use each instance's URL from the "
                "catalog (works with and without a shared port). Set = "
                "<base>/mcp/<id>, for a router running on another machine."
            ),
        )
        deny_instances: str = Field(
            default="mcp_manager_control",
            description="Comma-separated instance IDs the router must ignore entirely",
        )
        forward_user_identity: bool = Field(
            default=True,
            description=(
                "Pass the verified OpenWebUI user on to the target instance. "
                "Needs identity_mode=optional on this router; the target decides "
                "what it does with the identity."
            ),
        )
        allow_categories: str = Field(
            default="",
            description="Comma-separated categories to expose (empty = all)",
        )
        max_results: int = Field(
            default=60, description="Maximum number of function lines per answer"
        )
        cache_ttl: int = Field(
            default=60, description="Seconds the catalog is reused before refetching"
        )
        request_timeout: int = Field(
            default=60, description="Seconds to wait for a proxied tool call"
        )

    def __init__(self):
        self.valves = self.Valves()
        self._cache: list[dict] | None = None
        self._cache_time = 0.0

    # ── catalog ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def _denied(self) -> set[str]:
        names = {SELF_ID}
        names |= {p.strip() for p in self.valves.deny_instances.split(",") if p.strip()}
        return names

    async def _fetch_catalog(self) -> list[dict]:
        headers = {}
        if self.valves.auth_token:
            headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {self.valves.auth_token}"
        url = self.valves.manager_url.rstrip("/") + "/api/instances?include=specs"
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=15) as client:
            response = await client.get(url, headers=headers)
        response.raise_for_status()
        data = response.json()
        if not isinstance(data, list):
            raise RuntimeError("Unexpected manager response")
        if data and "specs" not in data[0]:
            # Guest payload: the allowlist dropped everything but the basics.
            raise RuntimeError(
                "Manager answered without specs — the auth_token valve is missing "
                "or wrong (an unauthenticated caller only gets the guest view)."
            )

        denied = self._denied()
        allowed = {c.strip().lower() for c in self.valves.allow_categories.split(",") if c.strip()}
        catalog = []
        for inst in data:
            if inst.get("status") != "running":
                continue  # the dashboard curates the catalog: stopped = invisible
            if inst.get("id") in denied:
                continue
            specs = inst.get("specs") or []
            if SELF_FINGERPRINT.issubset({s.get("name") for s in specs}):
                continue  # another router — calling it would be a loop
            if allowed and (inst.get("category") or "").lower() not in allowed:
                continue
            if not specs:
                continue
            catalog.append(inst)
        return catalog

    async def _catalog(self, force: bool = False) -> list[dict]:
        fresh = time.time() - self._cache_time < self.valves.cache_ttl
        if self._cache is not None and fresh and not force:
            return self._cache
        self._cache = await self._fetch_catalog()
        self._cache_time = time.time()
        return self._cache

    @staticmethod
    def _handles(catalog: list[dict]) -> dict[str, tuple[dict, dict]]:
        """`instance.tool` → (instance, spec) for every function in the catalog."""
        return {
            f"{inst['id']}.{spec['name']}": (inst, spec)
            for inst in catalog
            for spec in inst.get("specs") or []
            if spec.get("name")
        }

    # ── tools ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    async def find_tools(
        self, query_words: list[str] = None, category: str = "", mode: str = "or"
    ) -> str:
        """Directory of every tool available through this router. START HERE.

        Call it WITHOUT arguments to see the complete catalog — that is the
        cheap, safe default. Pass query_words only to narrow a large catalog
        down; a query that matches nothing returns everything instead of
        failing, so you can never end up empty-handed.

        Each line is "instance.action — what it does". Use that exact string
        with describe_tools() to get the parameters, then call_tool() to run
        it. This listing deliberately contains no parameter schemas.

        Args:
            query_words: Search terms, e.g. ["law", "gesetz"]. Full handles
                like "gesetze_im_internet.get_paragraph" and bare instance IDs
                are accepted too and count as direct hits.
            category: Restrict to one category (as shown in the listing)
            mode: "or" = any word matches (default, recommended),
                "and" = every word must match
        """
        try:
            catalog = await self._catalog()
        except Exception as e:
            return f"Could not read the catalog from the manager: {e}"
        if not catalog:
            return (
                "No instances available. Either none are running, or all of them "
                "are excluded by the deny_instances / allow_categories valves."
            )

        handles = self._handles(catalog)
        words = [w for w in (query_words or []) if str(w).strip()]
        notes: list[str] = []

        # Direct hits first: the model tends to pass the full identifier where
        # keywords are expected — that must be a hit, not a miss.
        direct: list[str] = []
        rest: list[str] = []
        for word in words:
            word = str(word).strip()
            if word in handles:
                direct.append(word)
                notes.append(f"'{word}' matched a tool directly")
            elif any(word == inst["id"] for inst in catalog):
                hits = [h for h in handles if h.startswith(word + ".")]
                direct.extend(hits)
                notes.append(f"'{word}' matched an instance ({len(hits)} tools)")
            else:
                parts = [p for p in _norm(word).replace(".", " ").replace("_", " ").split() if p]
                if len(parts) > 1:
                    notes.append(f"'{word}' split into: {', '.join(parts)}")
                rest.extend(parts)

        if category:
            wanted = _norm(category)
            catalog = [i for i in catalog if _norm(i.get("category") or "") == wanted]
            handles = self._handles(catalog)
            notes.append(f"category filter: {category}")

        selected = list(dict.fromkeys(direct))
        if rest:
            scored = []
            for handle, (inst, spec) in handles.items():
                haystack = _norm(" ".join([
                    inst.get("id", ""), inst.get("name", ""), inst.get("description", ""),
                    inst.get("category", ""), spec.get("name", ""), spec.get("description", ""),
                ]))
                hits = sum(1 for p in rest if p in haystack)
                if hits and (mode.lower() != "and" or hits == len(rest)):
                    scored.append((hits, handle))
            scored.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[0], x[1]))
            selected += [h for _, h in scored if h not in selected]

        matched = len(selected)
        if words and not selected:
            # A search must never be the gate the model gets stuck at.
            notes.append("no match for those words — showing the complete catalog")
        if not selected:
            selected = list(handles)

        limit = max(1, self.valves.max_results)
        shown, cut = selected[:limit], max(0, len(selected) - limit)
        logger.info(
            f"find_tools(query={words or '-'}, mode={mode}) -> {matched or len(selected)} "
            f"of {len(handles)} tools in {len(catalog)} instances"
        )

        header = (
            f"{len(handles)} tool{'' if len(handles) == 1 else 's'} in "
            f"{len(catalog)} instance{'' if len(catalog) == 1 else 's'}"
        )
        if words:
            header += f" · query: {', '.join(str(w) for w in words)} ({mode.upper()})"
            header += f" · {matched} match(es)"
        lines = [header]
        if notes:
            lines += [f"note: {n}" for n in notes]
        lines.append("")

        by_instance: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
        for handle in shown:
            by_instance.setdefault(handle.split(".", 1)[0], []).append(handle)
        for instance_id, group in by_instance.items():
            inst = handles[group[0]][0]
            # Name and description are optional in a config — don't print empty
            # separators or the ID twice.
            title = instance_id
            if inst.get("name") and inst["name"] != instance_id:
                title += f" — {inst['name']}"
            if inst.get("category"):
                title += f" [{inst['category']}]"
            summary = _first_line(inst.get("description"), 110)
            lines.append(f"{title}: {summary}" if summary else title)
            for handle in group:
                lines.append(f"  {handle} — {_first_line(handles[handle][1].get('description'))}")
            lines.append("")
        if cut:
            lines.append(f"({cut} more — narrow the search with query_words)")
        lines.append("Next: describe_tools([\"instance.action\"]) for the parameters,")
        lines.append('then call_tool(tool="instance.action", arguments={...}) to run it.')
        return "\n".join(lines)

    async def describe_tools(self, tools: list[str]) -> str:
        """Full parameter schema for one or more tools from find_tools().

        Pass the exact "instance.action" strings from the directory; several at
        once are fine. Do this before call_tool() — the directory intentionally
        omits schemas to keep it small.

        Args:
            tools: Handles, e.g. ["gesetze_im_internet.get_paragraph"]
        """
        try:
            catalog = await self._catalog()
        except Exception as e:
            return f"Could not read the catalog from the manager: {e}"
        handles = self._handles(catalog)

        logger.info(f"describe_tools({list(tools or [])})")
        blocks = []
        for raw in tools or []:
            handle = str(raw).strip()
            if handle not in handles:
                blocks.append(self._unknown_handle(handle, handles))
                continue
            _, spec = handles[handle]
            blocks.append(self._describe(handle, spec))
        if not blocks:
            return "No tools given. Call find_tools() to see what exists."
        return "\n\n".join(blocks)

    async def call_tool(self, tool: str, arguments: dict = None) -> str:
        """Run a tool from this router's catalog and return its result.

        This is the only way to run the tools listed by find_tools(). It is not
        the only way to reach those servers in general: if your client already
        has one of them registered as its own MCP server, calling it there is
        fine and cheaper — use this router for everything else.

        `tool` is a STRING VALUE, not a function you can call. "owui_rag.query_knowledge"
        is a handle that belongs in this parameter — calling it by that name directly
        will not work, no matter what your client suggests. The real parameters of the
        target tool go into `arguments` as a nested object:

            call_tool(tool="owui_rag.query_knowledge",
                      arguments={"query": "Meta-Modell", "knowledge": "Psychologie & Therapie"})

        If a call fails, fix the arguments and call this again — do not fall back to
        raw HTTP; there is no direct access to the instances from here.

        Args:
            tool: Handle from find_tools(), e.g. "gesetze_im_internet.get_paragraph"
            arguments: Object with the parameters from describe_tools(),
                e.g. {"law": "bgb", "paragraph": "823"}
        """
        handle = str(tool or "").strip()
        # The user id, never the token: this line ends up in a log file.
        try:
            from app.identity import get_current_identity
            caller = getattr(get_current_identity(), "sub", None)
        except ImportError:
            caller = None
        logger.info(
            f"call_tool({handle}, args={sorted((arguments or {}).keys())})"
            + (f" for {caller}" if caller else "")
        )
        instance_id = handle.split(".", 1)[0]
        # Checked before the catalog lookup: `tool` is free text, so a model
        # that knows or guesses the name must not slip past the deny list.
        if instance_id in self._denied():
            logger.warning(f"call_tool refused: '{instance_id}' is on the deny list")
            return f"Instance '{instance_id}' is not available through this router."

        try:
            catalog = await self._catalog()
        except Exception as e:
            return f"Could not read the catalog from the manager: {e}"
        handles = self._handles(catalog)
        if handle not in handles:
            logger.info(f"call_tool: unknown handle '{handle}'")
            return self._unknown_handle(handle, handles)

        inst, spec = handles[handle]
        try:
            return await self._invoke(inst, spec, handle, arguments or {})
        except Exception as first_error:
            # The instance may have moved to another port since the catalog was
            # cached (the manager reassigns busy ports on start). Refetch once.
            logger.warning(f"call_tool({handle}) failed ({first_error}) — refreshing catalog and retrying")
            try:
                catalog = await self._catalog(force=True)
            except Exception:
                return self._offline(handle, first_error)
            handles = self._handles(catalog)
            if handle not in handles:
                return (
                    f"'{handle}' is no longer available — the instance was stopped "
                    "or removed. Call find_tools() again."
                )
            inst, spec = handles[handle]
            try:
                return await self._invoke(inst, spec, handle, arguments or {})
            except Exception as second_error:
                return self._offline(handle, second_error)

    # ── internals ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def _caller_agent_token(self) -> str:
        """The token of the *agent* calling us, when the manager passes it down.

        Empty for a human caller (their identity travels as a user JWT), empty
        outside the framework, and empty unless this instance is configured to
        receive it. Never logged and never returned to a caller.
        """
        try:
            from app import identity as identity_module
            from app.identity import SOURCE_AGENT
        except ImportError:
            return ""
        who = identity_module.get_current_identity()
        if who is None or who.source != SOURCE_AGENT:
            return ""
        return who.raw_token or ""

    def _headers_for(self, inst: dict) -> dict:
        """Exactly two things travel to the target: this router's own bearer,
        and the caller's user token unchanged.

        The bearer says "this client may talk to that MCP server". The user
        token says who is asking — passed through as it arrived, so the target
        verifies it against the shared secret itself. This router vouches for
        nobody and decides nothing: the instance behind it is where access is
        granted or refused, and it must be able to do that without trusting
        anything the router adds.

        Deliberately not forwarded: cookies and every other header of the
        original request. The incoming Authorization is replaced by this
        router's own — with one exception, added on 03.09.: when the caller is
        a named *agent* and the manager hands its token down, that token is
        forwarded instead. Otherwise every agent would arrive at the target as
        the shared bearer, and an instance that decides by agent identity could
        not tell Claude Code from a cron job — which is the distinction agent
        identities exist for.
        """
        headers = {}
        if self.valves.mcp_token:
            headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {self.valves.mcp_token}"
        if not self.valves.forward_user_identity:
            return headers
        agent_bearer = self._caller_agent_token()
        if agent_bearer:
            # A named agent called us. Its own token goes on instead of ours,
            # so the target sees who is asking and applies its rules to that
            # agent rather than to "somebody holding the shared token". This
            # only ever happens when the manager hands the token down, which it
            # does for this instance alone (forward_agent_token in its config).
            headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {agent_bearer}"
            # And nothing else: an agent travels as a bearer, never as a user
            # token. Falling through to the block below would put it into the
            # user-JWT header, where the target tries to parse it as a JWT and
            # refuses with "malformed token" — found live on 03.09.
            return headers
        try:
            from app import identity as identity_module
        except ImportError:
            # The same tool JSON also runs inside OpenWebUI itself, where there
            # is no framework to ask. Without an identity there is nothing to
            # forward, which is not an error here — the target refuses if it
            # needs one.
            return headers
        who = identity_module.get_current_identity()
        if who is None:
            return headers
        if who.raw_token:
            headers[identity_module.header_name()] = who.raw_token
            return headers
        # Identity established from OpenWebUI's plain headers: there is no
        # token to hand on, so the same four headers are rebuilt. They are a
        # claim either way — this router adds no weight to them, it only keeps
        # the target from seeing an anonymous call where a user made it.
        plain = getattr(identity_module, "PLAIN_HEADERS", {})
        for claim, header in plain.items():
            value = getattr(who, claim, "")
            if value:
                headers[header] = str(value)
        return headers

    async def _invoke(self, inst: dict, spec: dict, handle: str, arguments: dict) -> str:
        from mcp import ClientSession

        base = self.valves.mcp_base_url.strip().rstrip("/")
        url = f"{base}/mcp/{inst['id']}" if base else inst.get("url")
        if not url:
            return f"No reachable address for '{inst['id']}'."
        headers = self._headers_for(inst)

        async with _mcp_streams(url, headers, self.valves.request_timeout) as (read, write):
            async with ClientSession(read, write) as session:
                init = await session.initialize()
                # serverInfo in mcp 1.x, server_info in 2.x — reading the wrong
                # one would not fail, it would silently skip the check below.
                info = getattr(init, "server_info", None) or getattr(init, "serverInfo", None)
                served = getattr(info, "name", "")
                if served and served != inst["id"]:
                    # Ports get reassigned and can be recycled: without this the
                    # call could silently land on a different instance.
                    return (
                        f"Address of '{inst['id']}' now serves '{served}' — the port was "
                        "reassigned. Call find_tools() again."
                    )
                result = await session.call_tool(spec["name"], arguments)

        text = "\n".join(
            getattr(part, "text", "") for part in (result.content or []) if getattr(part, "text", "")
        ).strip()
        failed = getattr(result, "is_error", None)  # 2.x
        if failed is None:
            failed = getattr(result, "isError", False)  # 1.x
        if failed:
            logger.info(f"{handle} returned an error — answering with its schema")
            # Answer with the schema attached so the model can fix the call in
            # one step instead of guessing.
            return f"{handle} reported an error:\n{text or '(no message)'}\n\n{self._describe(handle, spec)}"
        return text or "(empty result)"

    def _describe(self, handle: str, spec: dict) -> str:
        lines = [f"{handle}", (spec.get("description") or "").strip() or "(no description)"]
        params = (spec.get("parameters") or {}).get("properties") or {}
        required = set((spec.get("parameters") or {}).get("required") or [])
        if not params:
            lines.append("Parameters: none")
        else:
            lines.append("Parameters:")
            for name, schema in params.items():
                schema = schema if isinstance(schema, dict) else {}
                kind = schema.get("type") or "any"
                if isinstance(schema.get("enum"), list):
                    kind = " | ".join(str(v) for v in schema["enum"])
                flag = "required" if name in required else "optional"
                description = str(schema.get("description") or "").strip()
                default = f", default {schema['default']!r}" if "default" in schema else ""
                lines.append(f"  {name} ({kind}, {flag}{default}){': ' + description if description else ''}")
        example = {name: f"<{name}>" for name in params if name in required}
        lines.append(f'Call: call_tool(tool="{handle}", arguments={example})')
        return "\n".join(lines)

    @staticmethod
    def _unknown_handle(handle: str, handles: dict) -> str:
        near = difflib.get_close_matches(handle, list(handles), n=5, cutoff=0.4)
        if not near and "." in handle:
            prefix = handle.split(".", 1)[0]
            near = [h for h in handles if h.startswith(prefix + ".")][:5]
        hint = "\n".join(f"  {h}" for h in near)
        return (
            f"Unknown tool '{handle}'."
            + (f" Did you mean:\n{hint}" if near else "")
            + "\nCall find_tools() for the full directory."
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _offline(handle: str, error: Exception) -> str:
        return (
            f"'{handle}' could not be reached — the instance is most likely not "
            f"running anymore. Call find_tools() to see what is available.\n"
            f"(technical detail: {type(error).__name__}: {error})"
        )

specs.name: call_tool
specs.description:
Run a tool from this router's catalog and return its result.

This is the only way to run the tools listed by find_tools(). It is not
the only way to reach those servers in general: if your client already
has one of them registered as its own MCP server, calling it there is
fine and cheaper — use this router for everything else.

`tool` is a STRING VALUE, not a function you can call. "owui_rag.query_knowledge"
is a handle that belongs in this parameter — calling it by that name directly
will not work, no matter what your client suggests. The real parameters of the
target tool go into `arguments` as a nested object:

    call_tool(tool="owui_rag.query_knowledge",
              arguments={"query": "Meta-Modell", "knowledge": "Psychologie & Therapie"})

If a call fails, fix the arguments and call this again — do not fall back to
raw HTTP; there is no direct access to the instances from here.

arguments.description: Object with the parameters from describe_tools(), e.g. {"law": "bgb", "paragraph": "823"}

specs.name: describe_tools
specs.description:
Full parameter schema for one or more tools from find_tools().

Pass the exact "instance.action" strings from the directory; several at
once are fine. Do this before call_tool() — the directory intentionally
omits schemas to keep it small.

specs.name: find_tools
specs.description:
Directory of every tool available through this router. START HERE.

Call it WITHOUT arguments to see the complete catalog — that is the
cheap, safe default. Pass query_words only to narrow a large catalog
down; a query that matches nothing returns everything instead of
failing, so you can never end up empty-handed.

Each line is "instance.action — what it does". Use that exact string
with describe_tools() to get the parameters, then call_tool() to run
it. This listing deliberately contains no parameter schemas.

query_words.description: Search terms, e.g. ["law", "gesetz"]. Full handles like "gesetze_im_internet.get_paragraph" and bare instance IDs are accepted too and count as direct hits.

category.description: Restrict to one category (as shown in the listing)

mode.description: "or" = any word matches (default, recommended), "and" = every word must match

meta.description: One connection instead of many — search the tools of all running MCP instances, fetch a schema, call it. Keeps the tool list in the prompt small. Read-only.
